sentences.text: This petition is filed by the L.R's of one deceased Kum.Khyati Gupta D/o Sri.Rajesh Gupta, under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.2,43,00,000/- in respect of her death in Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 12.10.2024 at about 11.17 am when Khyati Gupta was riding the Scooter bearing Reg.No.DL-12/SE-2686 on Outer ring road, when she reached opposite to Ecospace Tech Park, Bengaluru city, at that time, driver of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51/AJ-8574, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed and dashed the Khyati Gupta's vehicle and caused the accident.
Due to (SCCH-12) 3 MVC No.9416/2024 impact she sustained fatal injuries and died on the way to the St. John's Hospital.
Postmortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to her family members.

Petitioners have spent huge amount for transportation of dead body,
last rituals and funeral expenses.
3. At the time of accident deceased was hale and healthy she was aged about 23 years and Engineer graduate.
She was working as a Software Engineer at Dell International services ltd., Bangalore and per pay scale was Rs.15,00,000/- p.a.
That deceased was the only earning member in the family, due to her untimely death petitioners are put to great financial hardship.
The accident is due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51/AJ-8574.
The Bellandur Traffic police have registered a case against the said driver in Crime No.112/2024 for the offence P/U/S 106(1) (281) of BNS.
The respondent No.1 being Insurer and respondent no.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
On all these grounds petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.2,43,00,000/- with costs and interest in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 & 2 are served.
They appeared through their respective counsel and filed written statement.
5. In the written statement Respondent No.1 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

It has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of 2 nd respondent in (SCCH-12) 4 MVC No.9416/2024 respect of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51/AJ-8574, the liability of it if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy and subject to valid and effective DL of the driver and with Rajesh Gupta vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18030796/
2 valid and effective permit and fitness certificate as per the provisions of Sec.147 of M.V. Act.

sentences.text: It denies the manner and involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
It is contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased, as she was riding the vehicle without valid D.L. on the date of the accident.
Further, age, occupation and income of deceased are denied.
On all these grounds 1 st respondent prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
6. In the written statement the Respondent No.2 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
He admitted the ownership of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51/AJ- 8574.
It is contended that, this respondent no.2 and BMTC entered into an agreement dated 16-12-2022 for supply of 921 Electric buses.

In view of the agreement executed with BMTC the respondent no.2 further entered into an Operation cum Maintenance agreement dated 22-05-2024 w.e.f. 13-03-2024 with Prowiz Man systems Pvt. Ltd., ("Prowiz").
Therefore the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51/AJ-8574 was under the control of Prowiz.
Hence, Prowiz is necessary party to the proceedings.
Further, the driver had valid D.L., FC and Permit to the said offending vehicle as on the date of accident and the policy was in force.
Hence, respondent no.1 has to indemnify the respondent no.2.

Further age,
occupation and income of (SCCH-12) 5 MVC No.9416/2024 deceased are denied.
On all these grounds respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, this court has framed following;
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the only LR's of one Khyati Gupta and competent persons to file this petition?
2. Whether petitioners prove that on 12.10.2024 at about 11:17 AM when one Khyati Gupta was riding scooter bearing Reg. No.DL-12-SE-2686 on extream left side of the road by observing traffic rules on outer ring road, when she reached opposite to ECO Space Tech Park one bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-AJ-8574 came in high speed in rash and negligent manner dashed to Khyati Gupta and caused accident due to which she sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot?
3.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4. What Order or Award?
ADDITIONAL ISSUE 5. Whether 1st respondent proves there is entire negligence of the deceased in the accident?
8. To prove their case, petitioner no.1 entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
Through him Ex.P.1 to P.23 documents are marked.
One Harisha K.L. the H.R. Manager of DELL International Services India Pvt. Ltd., got examined as P.W.2.

9. Heard learned counsel for both sides.
Perused records.

10. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.5 : In the Negative,
 Issue No.4 : As per final order,
 for the following;
 REASONS 11. ISSUE No.1 : Petitioners, to prove that they are LR's of Khyati Gupta 1st petitioner got examined as P.W.1.
In his affidavit he has stated that he is father of deceased.
2 nd petitioner is said to be mother of the deceased.
In support of the same he has produced aadhar cards of petitioners and deceased, at Ex.P10 to 12 which show deceased is the daughter of petitioners No.1 and 2 herein.
Respondents have not seriously disputed the relationship with the deceased.

Therefore on the basis of I.D cards and the oral evidence of P.W.1 this court comes to the conclusion that the petitioners are the LR's of Kum.Khyati Gupta and competent persons to file this petition.
Accordingly, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE No.2: According to petitioners driver of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51/AJ-8574, was negligent.
To prove the same, (SCCH-12) 7 MVC No.9416/2024 P.W.1 in his chief examination affidavit stated about the negligence of bus driver.

He relied upon the crime records i.e. FIR,
Complaint, Further statement of the complainant, Spot mahazar, Spot sketch, IMV report, Inquest report, PM report, and Charge sheet in that regard.
13. On perusal of those documents it can be seen that, 1st petitioner himself is first informant and he is not an eye witness to the incident.
On the same day of the accident, FIR is registered.

On perusal of spot mahazar, spot sketch and Charge sheet it disclose that, on the date, time and place of accident when deceased was riding the Scooter bearing Reg.No.DL-12/SE-2686 on Outer ring road,
opposite to Ecospace Tech Park, Bengaluru city, driver of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51/AJ-8574,
drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed deceased vehicle from right side and caused the accident.
Due to the impact of the accident she sustained fatal injuries and died on the way to the Hospital.
IMV report shows that right side major portion of the deceased vehicle got damaged in the accident and it is opined that accident was not due to any mechanical defects of both the motor vehicles.
Ex . P8
Postmortem report discloses that the death was due to skull fracture and intracranial haemorrhage as a result of head injury sustained.
14. After completion of investigation the Bellanduru Traffic Police have filed charge sheet against driver of Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51/AJ-8574, for the offence punishable u/Sec.281 (SCCH-12) 8

sentences.text: In the cross examination of PW1, he has denied the material suggestion that his daughter was negligent in riding the vehicle.

On perusal of the charge sheet it can be seen that there is CCTV footage record of the accident but both the parties have not made any efforts to produce the same.
15.
In the cross examination of PW1, 2nd respondent owner of the bus has suggested that in the Criminal case registered against he bus driver, he is acquitted which is pleaded ignorance by the PW1.
The said judgment of acquittal is not produced here.
1st respondent insurance company has stated that deceased herself tried to overtake the bus and she was 100% negligent in the accident.
The same is denied by PW1.
To counter the same, 1st respondent has not lead any evidence.
In fact there is no evidence from the respondent side at all.

Therefore by considering the documents available on record and evidence of PW.1 it is clear that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle Bus and due to the said accidental injuries,
daughter of the petitioners is died.
Accordingly, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above reasons, petitioners are entitled for compensation for the negligence of bus driver.
Respondents disputed the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
To prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners have produced Notarized D.L. card of the deceased at Ex.P.13.
It shows she was born on 26-07-2001.
As on the date of accident (SCCH-12) 9 MVC No.9416/2024 i.e. on 12.10.2024 deceased was aged 23 years.
Therefore it is considered that the deceased was aged 23 years at the time of accident.
17. In the petition it is mentioned that deceased was a Engineer Graduate and working as Software Engineer at Dell International Services ltd., Bangalore and earning Rs.15,00,000/- per annum.

To prove her income and occupation, the Petitioners have produced Notarized copies of Provisional Certificate, B. Tech. Certificate and it shows that the deceased had completed her Bachelor of Technology.
Her pay slip for the month of July 2024 to Oct-2024 are produced but her IT returns are not produced.
The records show that she was recently joined the services of the Dell company.
As per her pay slip her net pay after deductions for the month of July 2024- Rs.83,258/- August 2024- Rs.82,604/-, September 2024- Rs.84,922/- October 2024- Rs.1,06,151/-.
Her account statement is also produced which tallies with the salaries mentioned.
18. The HR Manager of the Dell services has been examined as PW2.
In his evidence he has stated that deceased had annual income of Rs.12,39,075/-.
He has admitted in the cross examination that 4,49,572/- was her salary and remaining amount was allowance.
He has produced attendance register of the deceased which shows she was regular to work.

Now it is necessary to notice that as per evidence on Rajesh Gupta vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18030796/
5 record, deceased was Engineer and worked in the Dell company from 17.07.2023 till the date of her death i.e. on 12.10.2024.

sentences.text: Though she worked for more than one year, her form16 and IT returns are not produced before this court.

But her pay slips show that amount of Rs.8,480/-, Rs. 6,161/-, Rs.
5,093/- were deducted from her salary for the month of July, August and September respectively for income tax.
Therefore it is clear that she was income tax assessee.
There is no contrary evidence from the other side regarding the employment of the deceased.
Keeping in mind the nature of job of the deceased as software Engineer, her pay slips, and income tax deductions, it is proper to consider her income as Rs.95,000/- per month.
Accordingly, income of the deceased is considered as Rs.95,000/- per month.
Petitioners being parents of the deceased, they are considered as dependents on her.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under;
20. Loss of dependency:
As per above finding, petitioners are held to be dependents on the deceased.
As per the Praney Sethi case future prospects of the deceased will have to be added to the monthly income.
In case of salaried persons 50% of the income has to be added to the monthly income to the age group below 40 years.
Age of the deceased in this case is 23 years at the time of accident.

Therefore, in the present case the monthly income of deceased is Rs.95,000/- + 47,500/-
= Rs.1,42,500/-.
Further deceased being unmarried  (half) of (SCCH-12) 11 MVC No.9416/2024 her income shall be deducted towards her personal expenses.

As such, loss of dependency of the petitioners due to the death of their family member is Rs.
1,53,90,000/-
21.
Loss of love and affection: Petitioners being L.R's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their daughter due to her death in the accident.
Therefore, for loss of love and affection compensation has to be granted.

There is no hard and fast rule in respect of measuring love and affection but, in the opinion of this court if amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded for loss of love and affection, the interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, amount of Rs. 50,000 /- is awarded.
22. Loss of filial Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Pranay Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ Rs.40,000/- and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/- respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.

As such, accident being taken place in the year 2024, under the head of loss of estate Rs.18,150/-, for funeral expenses Rs.18,150/- and for loss of consortium Rs. 48,400/-
(SCCH-12) 12 MVC No.9416/2024 each to petitioner No.1 & 2 is awarded.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation as under:

1. Loss of Dependency : 1,53,90,000/-
2. Loss of love & affection : 50,000/-

petitioner No. 1 and 2 ( Rs.48,400/- each)
4. Loss of estate : 18,150/-

TOTAL 1,55,73,100/-
Therefore, this tribunal holds that the petitioners are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.1,55,73,100/-.
Since 1st respondent has admitted the policy of insurance to the offending bus, it has to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to petitioners.
1st respondent contended that the amount of Rs.20,00,000/- is received by the petitioner as exgratia amount from employer of the deceased and the same may be deducted from the total compensation.
But it is necessary to notice that the said amount is no way concerned with the present Insurance Company as it is paying the compensation for the negligence of the driver of the insured vehicle.
Therefore, the said contention cannot be accepted.

Hence, I answer this Issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. ISSUE No.5:
1st respondent in his written statement contended that there is entire negligence of the deceased in the accident.
But he has not led any evidence in this case.
Therefore, he has not proved his contention.
Accordingly, this issue is answered in the Negative.
24. ISSUE No.4:
Petitioners have sought for compensation of Rs.2,43,00,000/- in respect of death of Khyati Gupta in road traffic accident.
They have not claimed any rate of interest on the compensation amount.
But as per the settled law, the interest that could be awarded on the compensation is only 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.
They being L.Rs of the deceased are entitled for compensation in the apportionment of 40:60.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs. 1,55,73,100/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.
